data.narrative:
Pyka is a Series B autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $40M to date. The broader peer universe comprises 8 private frontier-tech firms operating in similar verticals, including Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation. No public comparables exist in this nascent sector.

Valuation triangulation relied on a single applicable methodology: Stage-Progression analysis. This approach applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier—typical for Series B to next-stage advancement—to the $40M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $76M. A peer-median approach was not viable given insufficient narrow-stage cohorts within the Drones & Autonomous universe; applying an all-sector median would risk material distortion given heterogeneity in business models and maturity across the broader set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $65M (low) to $87M (high), centered on $76M. This narrow range reflects methodological constraints rather than high confidence; the single-method triangulation leaves material uncertainty around market multiples for early-stage autonomous systems companies. Key unknowns include unit economics validation, regulatory pathway clarity, and comparable exit multiples—none of which can be inferred from current-stage financials. The valuation should be stress-tested against capital efficiency metrics and nearest-peer funding rounds as additional data surfaces.
